title: UDX: add conversation and endpoint tables
description:
## Summary

Several UDX streams can share one UDP socket pair, so the enclosing UDP conversation counts them together and Statistics > Conversations cannot say how much traffic any single stream carried. On `udx_multi.pcap.gz`, already in the tree, the UDP table shows one conversation of 381 frames where there are three streams of 127 frames each.

This registers conversation and endpoint tables keyed on the stream index the dissector already assigns, so each stream becomes its own row with its own frame and byte counts, identified by the Stream ID column.

```
-z conv,udp   1 conversation    381 frames   227184 bytes
-z conv,udx   3 conversations   127 frames    75728 bytes each
```

3 x 127 = 381 and 3 x 75728 = 227184, so the split accounts for every frame and byte the UDP row reports.

## What changed

The tables read a new `udx` tap. Its payload is declared in a new `epan/dissectors/packet-udx.h` as `udx_info_t`, carrying the decoded fixed header, the stream index, the addresses and ports of the carrying datagram plus the SACK blocks. `UDX_MAX_SACK_BLOCKS` moves into that header with it.

`CONVERSATION_UDX` and `ENDPOINT_UDX` are appended to the enum in `epan/conversation.h`. Appended rather than inserted, so no existing value renumbers.

The stream index only exists while sequence analysis is on, the same condition under which `udx.stream` is absent from the tree, so the tables follow the existing `analyze_sequence_numbers` preference. There is a test for that.

Two notes on things a reviewer may reasonably query:

- Ports are reported as the UDP ports that carried the stream, since UDX has none of its own, which is why the filter callbacks return `udp.srcport` and friends.
- `ui/cli/tap-iousers.c` decides whether to print ports with a hardcoded comparison against TCP, UDP and SCTP rather than the registered `hide_ports` flag, so `tshark -z conv,udx` omits them, as it already does for `-z conv,dccp`. Left alone here to keep this change focused. Happy to fix it separately if you would like.

## A prerequisite leak fix (first commit)

Adding the first `-z conv,...` and `-z endpoints,...` tests to the suite ran those CLI taps under AddressSanitizer for the first time, which surfaced a pre-existing leak. The conversation and endpoint taps allocate a `conv_hash_t` per run whose `conv_array` alone reserves about 2 MB, then never freed any of it. `iousers_finish` freed only its wrapper struct. The endpoint tap registered no finish callback at all.

The first commit fixes that in `ui/cli/tap-iousers.c` and `ui/cli/tap-endpoints.c`, calling `reset_conversation_table_data` / `reset_endpoint_table_data` and freeing the filter string on finish. It stands on its own and is not specific to UDX. `tshark -z conv,udp` leaked the same way before it. The UDX tables and tests are the second commit. Happy to split it into its own MR if you would rather.

## Testing

Four cases added to `test/suite_dissection.py`: the three-versus-one conversation split, the frame and byte totals cross-checked against the UDP table, the endpoint rows with the direction split and the fallback when sequence analysis is turned off. Byte counts are asked for machine readable so the columns are plain integers rather than SI prefixed.

Rebased onto master after the sequence analysis and reassembly change landed. The only overlap was that test file, where the new sequence cases and these conversation cases both append to the same class, so both sets are kept. Rebuilt on the new base and re-verified on Ubuntu 24.04, gcc 13, Qt 6.4.2:

- `packet-udx.c` compiled with `-DENABLE_WERROR=ON`: 0 warnings, 0 errors.
- Full build including the Qt GUI: exit 0.
- UDX dissection cases: 22 passed, the baseline set, the new sequence cases and the 4 added here.
- Whole test suite: **1467 passed, 21 skipped, 0 failed**, after `ninja test-programs`.
- Clang ASAN build (`WIRESHARK_DEBUG_WMEM_OVERRIDE=simple`): `-z conv,udx`, `-z endpoints,udx`, `-z conv,udp` and `-z endpoints,udp` all exit clean with no LeakSanitizer report. The UDX cases pass.
- `check_apis.py`, `check_col_apis.py`, `check_tfs.py`, `check_val_to_str.py`, `check_typed_item_calls.py --all-checks` and `check_static.py`: 0 warnings each.
- `checkhf.pl`, `checkfiltername.pl` and `tools/validate-commit.py`: clean.

Two details checked rather than assumed while writing this. `CONV_ID_UNSET` is `UINT32_MAX` rather than 0, so stream 0 still renders in the Stream ID column. And `pinfo->srcport` is `uint32_t`, which is why `udx_info_t` uses 32-bit ports and stays clean under the conversion warnings.

A release notes entry is included under New and Updated Features.

## AI assistance

An AI assistant (Claude, Anthropic) was used while developing this change. The design, the review and the verification are mine. I will make any changes you ask for myself. Protocol behaviour was taken from the existing dissector and from the libudx source rather than from a model's description of it. Every number quoted above is from a real run against captures already in the tree.

Assisted-by: Claude (Anthropic)

## CI

The earlier red pipeline was the account validation shared runners require, not a real failure. GitLab reported "The pipeline failed due to the user not being verified" and produced zero jobs. That is now verified, so the pipeline on this push runs for real.

+/* packet-udx.h
+ * Routines for UDX dissection
+ * Copyright 2026, Prabakaran Sivakumar <zkasuran@gmail.com>
+ *
+ * Wireshark - Network traffic analyzer
+ * By Gerald Combs <gerald@wireshark.org>
+ * Copyright 1998 Gerald Combs
+ *
+ * SPDX-License-Identifier: GPL-2.0-or-later
+ */
+
+#ifndef __PACKET_UDX_H__
+#define __PACKET_UDX_H__
+
+#include "ws_symbol_export.h"
+
+#include <epan/conversation.h>
+
+#ifdef __cplusplus
+extern "C" {
+#endif /* __cplusplus */
+
+/* Bounds the SACK blocks carried per packet; data_offset caps the area at
+ * 255 bytes, i.e. 31 blocks. */
+#define UDX_MAX_SACK_BLOCKS 32
+
+/*
+ * Queued on the "udx" tap: one decoded UDX header, with the stream it belongs
+ * to and the addresses and ports of the datagram that carried it.
+ *
+ * Sequence and acknowledgement numbers count packets rather than bytes, so
+ * seq advances by one per packet whatever the payload size. Consumers that
+ * want a byte offset have to accumulate payload_len themselves.
+ */
+typedef struct udx_info {
+    uint32_t id;            /* the receiver's stream id, as carried on the wire */
+    uint32_t seq;           /* per-packet sequence counter */
+    uint32_t ack;           /* next seq expected from the peer */
+    uint32_t window;        /* sender's receive window, in bytes */
+    uint32_t payload_len;   /* payload bytes, excluding SACK blocks and padding */
+    uint32_t stream;        /* Wireshark UDX stream index, as in udx.stream */
+    uint32_t sport;         /* UDP source port of the carrying datagram */
+    uint32_t dport;         /* UDP destination port of the carrying datagram */
+    uint8_t  flags;         /* UDX type flags */
+    uint8_t  data_offset;   /* bytes between the fixed header and the payload */
+    address  ip_src;
+    address  ip_dst;
+    unsigned num_sack_blocks;
+    uint32_t sack_start[UDX_MAX_SACK_BLOCKS];
+    uint32_t sack_end[UDX_MAX_SACK_BLOCKS];
+} udx_info_t;
+
+#ifdef __cplusplus
+}
+#endif /* __cplusplus */
+
+#endif /* __PACKET_UDX_H__ */
+

+ * Editor modelines  -  https://www.wireshark.org/tools/modelines.html
+ *
+ * Local variables:
+ * c-basic-offset: 4
+ * tab-width: 8
+ * indent-tabs-mode: nil
+ * End:
+ *
+ * vi: set shiftwidth=4 tabstop=8 expandtab:
+ * :indentSize=4:tabSize=8:noTabs=true:
+ */

@@ -1579,6 +1579,70 @@ class TestDissectUdx:
             ), encoding='utf-8', env=test_env)
         assert grep_output(stdout, 'Tail loss probe')
 
+    def test_udx_conversations_split_multiplexed_streams(self, cmd_tshark, capture_file, test_env):
+        '''Three streams on one socket pair are three UDX conversations.
+
+        The enclosing UDP flow counts them together, so the UDP table shows a
+        single conversation for the same capture.
+        '''
+        def rows(table):
+            stdout = subprocess.check_output((cmd_tshark, *UDX_HEUR,
+                    '-r', capture_file('udx_multi.pcap.gz'),
+                    '-q', '-z', table,
+                ), encoding='utf-8', env=test_env)
+            return [l for l in stdout.splitlines() if '<->' in l]
+
+        assert len(rows('conv,udp')) == 1
+        assert len(rows('conv,udx')) == 3
+
+    def test_udx_conversation_totals(self, cmd_tshark, capture_file, test_env):
+        '''The streams account for exactly what the UDP conversation carried.
+
+        Each of the three streams reports 127 frames and 75728 bytes, which adds
+        up to the 381 frames and 227184 bytes the UDP table reports for the whole
+        capture. Byte counts are asked for machine readable so the columns are
+        plain integers rather than SI prefixed.
+        '''
+        def total(table):
+            stdout = subprocess.check_output((cmd_tshark, *UDX_HEUR,
+                    '-r', capture_file('udx_multi.pcap.gz'),
+                    '-o', 'conv.machine_readable:TRUE',
+                    '-q', '-z', table,
+                ), encoding='utf-8', env=test_env)
+            rows = [l.split() for l in stdout.splitlines() if '<->' in l]
+            return [(int(r[7]), int(r[8])) for r in rows]
+
+        assert total('conv,udx') == [(127, 75728)] * 3
+        assert total('conv,udp') == [(381, 227184)]
+
+    def test_udx_endpoints(self, cmd_tshark, capture_file, test_env):
+        '''Both ends appear once, with the traffic split by direction.'''
+        stdout = subprocess.check_output((cmd_tshark, *UDX_HEUR,
+                '-r', capture_file('udx_multi.pcap.gz'),
+                '-o', 'conv.machine_readable:TRUE',
+                '-q', '-z', 'endpoints,udx',
+            ), encoding='utf-8', env=test_env)
+        rows = [l.split() for l in stdout.splitlines() if l.startswith('10.0.0.')]
+        assert [(r[0], int(r[1]), int(r[2])) for r in rows] == [
+            ('10.0.0.1', 381, 227184),
+            ('10.0.0.2', 381, 227184),
+        ]
+        # Sent one way is received the other.
+        assert (int(rows[0][3]), int(rows[0][4])) == (int(rows[1][5]), int(rows[1][6]))
+
+    def test_udx_conversations_follow_analysis_preference(self, cmd_tshark, capture_file, test_env):
+        '''The tables carry the stream index, so they need sequence analysis.
+
+        With the preference off the dissector assigns no stream number, the same
+        condition under which udx.stream is absent from the tree.
+        '''
+        stdout = subprocess.check_output((cmd_tshark, *UDX_HEUR,
+                '-r', capture_file('udx_multi.pcap.gz'),
+                '-oudx.analyze_sequence_numbers:FALSE',
+                '-q', '-z', 'conv,udx',
+            ), encoding='utf-8', env=test_env)
+        assert len([l for l in stdout.splitlines() if '<->' in l]) == 0
+

commits_data.title: tshark: free conversation and endpoint tap tables on exit
commits_data.message:
tshark: free conversation and endpoint tap tables on exit

The CLI conversation and endpoint taps allocate a conv_hash_t per run,
whose conv_array reserves room for 10000 items (about 2 MB), plus a
hashtable and a deep copy of every address. None of it was ever freed.
iousers_finish freed only the io_users_t wrapper. The endpoint tap
registered no finish callback at all.

It went unnoticed because nothing exercised these taps under
AddressSanitizer. Adding the first "-z conv,..." and "-z endpoints,..."
tests surfaced it: LeakSanitizer reported about 2 MB leaked per run and
failed the job.

Call reset_conversation_table_data and reset_endpoint_table_data from the
finish callbacks and free the filter string, so "tshark -z conv,<proto>"
and "tshark -z endpoints,<proto>" leave nothing behind.

Assisted-by: Claude (Anthropic)
AI-Assisted: yes (Claude, Anthropic)
